chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fazzal, from Ali ibn Asbat, from his uncle Ya'qub ibn Salim, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The example of the righteous woman is the example of the chough (a type of crow) which is rarely found. It was said, 'And what is the chough which is rarely found?' He (peace be upon him) said: 'One of its legs is white.'

key_terms.الْغُرَابِ الْأَعْصَمِ: The chough (a crow-like bird known for being rare or distinctive)
key_terms.لَا يَكَادُ يُقْدَرُ عَلَيْهِ: Rarely found / hard to come by

ai.seo_question: What is the metaphorical meaning of the righteous woman being compared to a chough with one white leg?
ai.summary: In *Al-Kafi*, Shaykh al-Kulayni records this narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to illustrate the scarcity of righteous women, employing the metaphor of the 'white-legged chough' (al-ghurab al-aṣam). This specific bird, known for its rarity and distinctive white leg, symbolizes a woman whose virtue stands out distinctly amidst the general population, emphasizing the high value placed on female piety in Shia tradition. The metaphor underscores that true righteousness is a rare and precious quality, much like the unique physical trait of this specific bird.
